title: Climbing Stairs
statement: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each move, you can climb either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
keyInsights: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), since the last move is either 1 or 2 steps
Only the previous two values are needed, so space can be O(1)
hintLadder: Write out the answers for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Do you see a pattern?
Think about the very last move you make to reach step n. Where could you have been just before it?
ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). Build it bottom-up, keeping only the last two values.
